findings.shape: A selected pollen-bearing male cycad has a short rough caudex with old leaf-base cues, a crown of arching pinnate fronds, narrow stiff spine-tipped leaflets with rolled-margin cues and an upright elongated pale pollen-cone study.
findings.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
findings.movement: Same retained woody axes, rachises, leaves and reproductive surfaces during small authored external deflection. Root/support position and scale remain anchored. Timing and angles are qualitative; there is no wind/elasticity solver, physiological simulation or measured biomechanics. Complete germination, organ emergence and seed-to-adult development are unavailable; no resizing of a ready mature plant.
findings.evidenceScope: Selected actual university living-plant account through search read: short trunk, arching pinnate fronds, separate-sex plants; female leafy megasporophyll head differs from compact male pollen cone. No palm/flower representation. Selected Flora of China species diagnosis through web retrieval; adult leaf, shoot and reproductive descriptions inform selected morphology, not numerical dynamics. Direct local HTML failed; no local full-text reading claimed.
corrections: Added a caudex with persistent old-leaf-base cues, separate pinnate fronds and narrow curved/revolute leaflet cues.
Varied frond rise and terminal height after the first overly uniform umbrella silhouette.
Replaced fan-like separated cone geometry with a closed elongated selected male pollen form, connected its peduncle, exposed the apex above foliage and improved the reproductive camera.
findings.residual: The male form does not represent the different female leafy megasporophyll structure. Old leaf bases remain angular, leaflets too regular, and cone sporophyll details much smoother than the authentic photograph. Revolute margins, stomata, petiole spines, scale/hair microstructure and optics are partial/unmeasured. No fertilization, full development or validated wind mechanics.
